title: MINOR: Stop the heartbeat thread when it fails with a fenced instance id
body:
When a heartbeat gets `FENCED_INSTANCE_ID`, the heartbeat thread sets
its failure cause. Its loop then disables the thread and waits on the
coordinator monitor. The thread does not exit.

The next `AbstractCoordinator.pollHeartbeat` call sees the failure, sets
`heartbeatThread` to null, and throws the cause. It does not close the
thread. A later `close()` calls `closeHeartbeatThread()`, which finds a
null reference and returns. So the thread
`kafka-coordinator-heartbeat-thread | <group>` waits until the JVM exits.
An application that recreates consumers after this error collects one
such thread per consumer.

The other fatal heartbeat errors (authentication, group authorization,
interrupt, unexpected errors) leave the run loop, so those threads end.

This change makes `pollHeartbeat` close the failed thread before it
drops the reference. `pollHeartbeat` already holds the coordinator
monitor, and `HeartbeatThread.close()` sets the closed flag and notifies
that monitor. The thread wakes up, sees that it is closed, and returns.
`pollHeartbeat` does not join the thread, so it does not block.

Testing: `testHeartbeatRequestWithFencedInstanceIdException` now closes
the coordinator after the fenced error and waits up to 2 seconds for the
heartbeat thread to stop. Without the fix, this test fails because the
thread is still alive. With the fix, it passes. `AbstractCoordinatorTest`,
`EagerConsumerCoordinatorTest`, `CooperativeConsumerCoordinatorTest`, and
`KafkaConsumerTest` pass.

I ran the tests at trunk commit f568b7b. There, `AbstractCoordinator.java`
and `BaseHeartbeatThread.java` are the same as on current trunk.
`AbstractCoordinatorTest.java` differs only by the KAFKA-20858 rename in
its setup (`SubscriptionState` to `ConsumerSubscriptionState`).
